lines: CORP\jdoe is LOCKED OUT since 2026-10-20 18:34 UTC (recorded by DC01).
This domain's policy locks an account out after 5 bad passwords within 30 minutes, for 30 minutes.
Most bad passwords came from PC123 (192.0.2.50): 8 failed sign-ins, 1 lockout in the last 24 h, the last at 2026-10-20 18:44 UTC.
PC123 kept trying after the account was locked out (3 times): something on it still has the old password, so the account will lock out again after an unlock.
EXCH01 is a mail server (ad_lockout_exchange_servers): a phone or a mail app (ActiveSync, Outlook) with the old password - update the password on the phone, or remove the account from it until then.
EXCH01 is not in this job's inventory: check it by hand (below).
WS9: something on it opens a share, a mapped drive or an application with the old password.
WS9 is not in this job's inventory: check it by hand (below).
On PC123: the service BackupAgent (Backup Agent - Running, Auto) logs on as CORP\jdoe - type the new password in services.msc > Log On, or give it a service account.
On PC123: the service Sync (Sync - Stopped, Manual) logs on as CORP\jdoe - type the new password in services.msc > Log On, or give it a service account.
On PC123: the scheduled task \Copy reports runs as CORP\jdoe - update its password in Task Scheduler (Properties > Change User or Group), or give it a service account.
On PC123: CORP\jdoe has a DISCONNECTED session (Disc, idle 1+02:00, logged on 10/19/2026 9:00 AM) - it keeps the old password: sign it out (quser, then logoff 3).
On PC123: OUTLOOK runs as CORP\jdoe (2 running) - an application holding the old password: close it or sign out.
On PC123: CORP\jdoe has drive H: mapped to \\files\home\jdoe - remove it and map it again with the new password (net use H: /delete).

To check a computer by hand: services (Log On As), Task Scheduler (Run as), Credential Manager (Windows Credentials) of the user, mapped drives (net use), disconnected Remote Desktop sessions (quser), applications with a saved password (Outlook, VPN, a phone's mail or Wi-Fi). On the user's own PC: lock it, and unlock it with the new password.
